titleText.es: Por lo general soy una persona bastante frugal, pero sigo comprándome de forma compulsiva cualquier aeronave teledirigida que cueste menos de $30. En los últimos años esto se ha convertido en un problema.
titleText.en: I'm normally a pretty frugal person, but I still compulsively buy any R/C aircraft that's less than $30. In the last few years, this has become a problem.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive expands the title text's R/C description as aeronave teledirigida and otherwise preserves the meaning of the official title text.

regions.labelEs: LÍNEA DEL TIEMPO DE LOS USOS COMERCIALES DE LAS BATERÍAS DE LITIO

applications.explanationEn: Línea names the line, and the fixed del tiempo completes the Spanish expression for a timeline.
The noun usos comes first and the describing word comerciales follows it.
Comerciales is plural to match usos; this adjective has the same plural form for masculine and feminine nouns.
Baterías is plural, de introduces the material, and litio remains singular.
The noun gente comes first and rica follows it as the description.
Rica is feminine singular because it matches the grammatically feminine singular word gente.

regions.labelEs: AVIONES Y HELICÓPTEROS POR RC. REALMENTE BARATOS. $10

excludedUnits.rationale: RC is the unchanged technical abbreviation for remote control rather than a Spanish lexical word.
The toy-box price is numeric notation rather than a Spanish lexical word.

applications.exampleEs: AVIONES Y HELICÓPTEROS POR RC. REALMENTE BARATOS
applications.explanationEn: Baratos is masculine plural because it describes the two masculine plural aircraft nouns together.
Real has the same masculine and feminine form, so adding -mente forms realmente, which strengthens baratos.

regions.labelEs: LA VIDA SERÍA MUCHO MEJOR SI FUERA UNO DE ESOS TIPOS QUE ENVEJECEN HACIA ATRÁS

applications.explanationEn: Ser keeps its full dictionary form and adds -ía to make the one-person-or-thing ‘would’ form.
Sería gives the imagined result, si introduces the unreal condition, and fuera is ser's hypothetical past form inside that condition.
Mucho goes before the comparative mejor to mean ‘much better’; muy would not fit this pattern.
Uno names one male person, de links him to the larger group, and esos tipos names that plural group.
Tipos names the people, que opens the information about them, and envejecen states what they do.
Hacia and atrás work together to express movement or development in a backward direction.

cards.noteEn: Línea means a line. In línea del tiempo, the three words together name a timeline.

example.es: La línea del tiempo empieza en 1900.
example.en: The timeline begins in 1900.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “timeline” in Spanish?
cards.noteEn: Del is the required contraction of de + el inside this fixed expression.

example.es: Dibujamos una línea del tiempo de la historia.
example.en: We drew a timeline of history.

cards.promptEs: baterías de litio · usos comerciales · envejecer hacia atrás
cards.questionEn: What development makes the reverse-aging wish funny?
cards.answerEn: Lithium batteries moved from specialized medical uses into phones and then inexpensive remote-controlled aircraft. The speaker wishes he could become younger as the increasingly appealing toys become cheap and widely available.
cards.noteEn: The title text confirms that the speaker compulsively buys inexpensive remote-controlled aircraft.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of línea del tiempo, “timeline”
cards.noteEn: Del combines de and el. It is the required middle word in línea del tiempo.

example.es: Añadieron una fecha a la línea del tiempo.
example.en: They added a date to the timeline.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

example.es: Necesito una mochila nueva.
example.en: I need a new backpack.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: Comerciales is plural. The same form works with masculine and feminine plural nouns.

example.es: Estudian los usos comerciales del invento.
example.en: They study the commercial uses of the invention.

cards.questionEn: How do you name a lithium battery in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Use batería de litio for one or baterías de litio for more than one.
cards.noteEn: The material name stays singular after de.

example.es: El aparato usa una batería de litio.
example.en: The device uses a lithium battery.

cards.answerEn: of; made of or from (introducing a material)
cards.noteEn: After an object or an expression such as ser de or estar hecho de, de introduces the material that composes it.

example.es: La puerta es de metal.
example.en: The door is made of metal.

cards.noteEn: Marcapasos has the same written form for one pacemaker and for several; the surrounding words show the number.

example.es: El marcapasos regula el ritmo del corazón.
example.en: The pacemaker regulates the heart's rhythm.

cards.noteEn: Here móviles stands by itself as the plural noun for mobile or cell phones, with teléfonos understood.

example.es: Los móviles nuevos duran más.
example.en: The new cell phones last longer.

cards.noteEn: Rica matches the feminine singular noun gente even though gente refers to multiple people.

example.es: La gente rica vivía en ese barrio.
example.en: Rich people lived in that neighborhood.

cards.noteEn: Por can introduce the means or system through which something is controlled. Here the following abbreviation names remote control.

example.es: El juguete funciona por control remoto.
example.en: The toy works by remote control.

cards.questionEn: How do you turn many describing words into words such as “quickly,” “clearly,” or “probably”?
cards.answerEn: Use the feminine singular form of the describing word and add -mente. If its masculine and feminine forms are identical, simply add -mente.
cards.noteEn: For an adjective that changes, use its -a form: claro becomes clara and then claramente. For one form shared by both genders, probable becomes probablemente. The new word usually describes how an action happens or how the speaker judges a claim.

example.es: Lucía responde claramente.
example.en: Lucía answers clearly.

cards.noteEn: As a time label, el presente contrasts with el pasado, the past.

example.es: La gráfica llega hasta el presente.
example.en: The chart reaches the present.

cards.noteEn: Sería is the “would” form of ser, “to be.” Spanish keeps the full dictionary form ser and adds -ía.

example.es: Sería una buena solución.
example.en: It would be a good solution.

cards.questionEn: How do you form a Spanish “would” verb such as “would forget”?
cards.answerEn: Keep the whole dictionary form and add a conditional ending such as -ía.
cards.noteEn: The same endings attach to verbs ending in -ar, -er, and -ir. The ending changes for the person: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, or -ían.

example.es: Viajaríamos en tren.
example.en: We would travel by train.

cards.questionEn: How do you describe an imagined “if…, …would…” situation?
cards.answerEn: Use si followed by a hypothetical past verb form for the condition, and use a “would” form for the result.
cards.noteEn: Spanish calls the condition's verb form the imperfect subjunctive. It often ends in -ra or -se, as in tuviera or tuviese. The result uses the conditional, often ending in -ría, as in haría. In this pattern, do not put the conditional directly after si.

example.es: Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más.
example.en: If I had time, I would travel more.

cards.noteEn: Put mucho before a comparison such as mejor or peor to make the difference stronger. Do not use muy in this pattern.

example.es: Esta opción es mucho mejor.
example.en: This option is much better.

cards.questionEn: How do you strengthen a comparison such as mejor or peor?
cards.answerEn: Put mucho before the comparative: mucho mejor, mucho peor, mucho más fácil.
cards.noteEn: Use mucho rather than muy before a comparative form.

example.es: La segunda ruta es mucho más corta.
example.en: The second route is much shorter.

cards.noteEn: Mejor compares one option with another. It does not change for gender: una solución mejor and un plan mejor both use mejor.

example.es: Necesitamos una idea mejor.
example.en: We need a better idea.

cards.answerEn: were; were the case, in an unreal condition
cards.noteEn: Fuera is a special form of ser used for a hypothetical situation. In si no fuera por..., it introduces something without which the result would be different. Do not confuse it with fuera meaning “outside.”

example.es: Si fuera fácil, todos lo harían.
example.en: If it were easy, everyone would do it.

cards.questionEn: How do you identify one member of a larger group?
cards.answerEn: Use uno or una, then de, then name the plural group.
cards.noteEn: Choose uno or una to match the understood member. A demonstrative or article may appear before the plural group: uno de esos libros, una de las profesoras.

example.es: Ella es una de las mejores jugadoras.
example.en: She is one of the best players.

cards.answerEn: of; links one member to a larger group
cards.noteEn: After uno or una, de introduces the group that the one member belongs to.

example.es: Es uno de mis vecinos.
example.en: He is one of my neighbors.

cards.noteEn: Esos points to masculine plural people or things that are not right beside the speaker. It changes to esas before feminine plural nouns.

example.es: Esos libros son nuevos.
example.en: Those books are new.

cards.noteEn: Tipo can informally mean a person or guy. The plural tipos may refer to a group of men or a mixed group.

example.es: Conozco a unos tipos que trabajan aquí.
example.en: I know some guys who work here.

cards.questionEn: How do you add information about a named person or thing using “who,” “that,” or “which”?
cards.answerEn: Put que after the person or thing, then add a verb and the information about it.
cards.noteEn: Que links the added description to the person or thing before it. It does not change for masculine, feminine, singular, or plural nouns. The added part needs a verb: la casa que vimos means “the house that we saw.”

example.es: La casa que vimos es azul.
example.en: The house that we saw is blue.

cards.noteEn: Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.noteEn: Envejecen is the present-time form for more than one person or thing.

example.es: Algunas personas envejecen lentamente.
example.en: Some people age slowly.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that movement, direction, or progress goes backward?
cards.noteEn: Hacia supplies the direction and atrás points toward the back or reverse. The phrase can describe physical movement or an abstract process.

example.es: El vídeo va hacia atrás.
example.en: The video is going backward.
